title: Add a persistent policy for handing clicked links to the system browser
before: At first parent 58c896ea4ebaff5425a068f461b6c6fedadb8b40, an ordinary HTTP(S) click handled by ExternalLink reached openLink and opened an in-app preview. The system browser was selected only for an explicit native request, the platform open-elsewhere modifier or middle click, connector authorization links, HUD links, and non-HTTP(S) schemes. There was no stored user preference or settings control that changed the ordinary-click destination.
after: At pinned merge 074349fb2744eacafbf80234444541aa736b1689, the desktop renderer owns an off-by-default, localStorage-backed boolean preference synchronized across open windows. A localized settings toggle changes that preference. The central clicked-link dispatcher consults it and, when enabled, sends normalized links through the existing operating-system browser bridge without creating an in-app preview. When disabled, prior routing remains intact. Explicit context-menu actions continue to invoke in-app preview or external handoff directly and are not overridden by the ordinary-click preference.
diff: Relative to first parent 58c896ea4ebaff5425a068f461b6c6fedadb8b40, the merge changes 9 desktop files with 101 insertions and 1 deletion: it adds the preference store and its persistence/cross-window tests; adds a settings toggle plus typed English, Russian, and Chinese copy; imports the preference into the central link dispatcher and adds it to the external-handoff guard; and adds a component test proving that an enabled preference sends a plain web-link click externally and leaves the preview collection empty.

episode.title: Add a persistent policy for handing clicked links to the system browser
episode.before: At first parent 58c896ea4ebaff5425a068f461b6c6fedadb8b40, an ordinary HTTP(S) click handled by ExternalLink reached openLink and opened an in-app preview. The system browser was selected only for an explicit native request, the platform open-elsewhere modifier or middle click, connector authorization links, HUD links, and non-HTTP(S) schemes. There was no stored user preference or settings control that changed the ordinary-click destination.
episode.after: At pinned merge 074349fb2744eacafbf80234444541aa736b1689, the desktop renderer owns an off-by-default, localStorage-backed boolean preference synchronized across open windows. A localized settings toggle changes that preference. The central clicked-link dispatcher consults it and, when enabled, sends normalized links through the existing operating-system browser bridge without creating an in-app preview. When disabled, prior routing remains intact. Explicit context-menu actions continue to invoke in-app preview or external handoff directly and are not overridden by the ordinary-click preference.
episode.diff: Relative to first parent 58c896ea4ebaff5425a068f461b6c6fedadb8b40, the merge changes 9 desktop files with 101 insertions and 1 deletion: it adds the preference store and its persistence/cross-window tests; adds a settings toggle plus typed English, Russian, and Chinese copy; imports the preference into the central link dispatcher and adds it to the external-handoff guard; and adds a component test proving that an enabled preference sends a plain web-link click externally and leaves the preview collection empty.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned ref 074349fb2744eacafbf80234444541aa736b1689 is the merge of PR #120790, titled as a desktop setting to always open links in the external browser; its first parent is 58c896ea4ebaff5425a068f461b6c6fedadb8b40.

The first-parent change comprises 9 desktop files, 101 insertions, and 1 deletion, including a new preference store, store tests, routing integration, routing tests, settings UI, and localization entries.

The new renderer-owned preference defaults to false, is stored under hermes.desktop.alwaysExternalLinks.v1, persists every atom update, and reacts to matching browser storage events so other open windows adopt the stored value.
Store tests assert the preference defaults off, persists both true and false transitions, and follows a matching storage event from another window.
The configuration settings surface subscribes to the preference and renders a ToggleRow whose change handler updates it.
The translation contract and English, Russian, and Chinese locales add a title and description explaining both ordinary-click external routing and the continuing explicit in-app-browser command.

The central openLink decision now reads the preference after URL normalization and before the existing authorization, HUD, and scheme guards; a true value selects openExternalLink, while a false value leaves the existing preview branch reachable.

ExternalLink intercepts ordinary anchor clicks, preserves consumer cancellation, derives an explicit native request from the component flag or modifier keys, and delegates the final destination decision to openLink.
In the first-parent version, the openLink external-routing guard did not consult any stored preference, so a normal HTTP(S) click fell through to the lazy in-app preview branch.

The pre-existing routing test establishes the baseline contract: a plain web-link click does not call the external bridge and instead creates an in-app preview; a modifier click calls the external bridge and creates no preview.
The added routing test enables the preference, performs a plain click, expects the operating-system bridge to receive the normalized URL, and expects the preview collection to remain empty.
Explicit context-menu choices bypass ordinary-click routing: Open in in-app browser calls openPreview directly, while Open in external browser calls openExternalLink directly.
Context-menu tests assert that both explicit destinations are offered for an ordinary chat link and that selecting Open in in-app browser creates a preview for the selected URL.

title: Route macOS workspace launches through an encoded application deep link
before: At parent commit 12c37a6b5cdb3fff2c03a355ca9948866bf1df07, the macOS launcher invoked `open -a <app_path> <workspace>`, passing the workspace as a macOS document-open argument. The resolution commit explains that recent desktop builds could focus the application without honoring that folder argument, so `codex app [PATH]` could fail to open the requested workspace.
after: At commit f94c49cf465b7403f22894f2db1432dee66fd64e, the launcher converts the workspace path into the `path` query parameter of a `codex://threads/new` URL using form URL encoding, then passes that URL to `open -a <app_path>`. Its failure message reports the same URL handed to the operating system. A unit test parses a deep link built from a path containing a space and `#` and confirms that the scheme, host, route, and decoded query value preserve the intended workspace.
diff: The single changed file, `codex-rs/cli/src/desktop_app/mac.rs`, adds `codex_new_thread_url`, which lossily converts the platform path to text, serializes it as a `path` query pair, and prefixes the query with `codex://threads/new?`. `open_codex_app` now constructs this URL and supplies it to the existing `open -a` subprocess instead of supplying the raw workspace path; the nonzero-exit diagnostic is updated accordingly. The same file adds `codex_new_thread_url_encodes_workspace_path`, covering URL parsing and query round-trip behavior for reserved characters. Existing upstream call sites still canonicalize the requested CLI path when possible and route both already-installed and newly-installed application launches through `open_codex_app`.

commit.subject: Use deep links for macOS codex app paths (#25485)
commit.body_excerpt:
## Why

`codex app [PATH]` is the documented CLI entry point for opening Codex
Desktop on a workspace. Recent desktop builds can focus the app while
failing to honor paths passed as macOS document-open arguments via `open
-a Codex.app <workspace>`, which broke `codex app .` for users. See
#25333; related report: #25166.

The desktop app still supports the explicit
`codex://threads/new?path=...` route, so the CLI should use that
app-owned launch surface instead of depending on folder-open event
delivery.

## What Changed

- Build a `codex://threads/new?path=<workspace>` URL in the macOS app
launcher.
- Pass that URL to `open -a <Codex.app>` instead of passing the
workspace path as a document argument.
- Add coverage that workspace paths needing escaping round-trip through
URL query encoding.

## Verification

- `just test -p codex-cli codex_new_thread_url_encodes_workspace_path`

candidate_workflows.title: Make repeated empty-state documentation handoffs user-controlled
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order resolution chain for removing unwanted automatic browser launches from a reusable empty-state status path while preserving link accessibility and establishing a deterministic regression oracle.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure repeated empty-state status requests provide actionable documentation guidance without automatically opening browser tabs.
when_to_use: A command, status view, refresh path, or similarly repeatable interaction automatically opens documentation when no resources are configured.
Multiple callers converge on the same empty-state branch, making an otherwise helpful browser handoff repeatable.
The external documentation target should remain available, but navigation should require deliberate user action.
anti_goals: Do not remove or silently change the established documentation target.
Do not alter configured-resource status, discovery, authentication, or refresh behavior beyond the shared empty-state return path.
Do not optimize browser-launch mechanics or add another environment-specific automatic-launch policy.
Do not claim that the external URL destination or the internal documentation command itself was exercised unless separately validated.
not_applicable_when: Automatic browser navigation is the explicit primary operation requested by the user rather than an incidental empty-state side effect.
The path is guaranteed to execute only once and product requirements explicitly require immediate browser launch.
No stable link, internal route, or other actionable handoff can be supplied to the user.
The observed tab opening originates outside the inspected status-response boundary.
inputs: The empty-state predicate for the relevant resource collections.
All command or refresh call sites that reach the shared status-response boundary.
A command-level test fixture capable of producing the empty state.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A repeatable shared status path automatically launches external documentation in at least one environment when its resource collections are empty, and its tests encode environment-specific opener behavior.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Every inspected caller reaching the empty state receives the same actionable informational response; the preserved documentation target and internal alternative are visible, no automatic browser invocation remains in that branch, and a deterministic unit test guards the response contract.

steps.condition: Apply when the shared empty-state branch owns an incidental automatic browser handoff and must continue directing users to documentation.
steps.validation: The implementation has no browser-opener import or invocation for the empty state, preserves the documentation URL, supplies `/docs` as an alternative, and leaves non-empty status logic outside the diff.

steps.condition: Apply after the empty-state result has been made environment-independent.
steps.validation: With an empty configured-resource map, the command test asserts the exact informational handoff response without mocking or expecting a browser opener.

validation_ladder: Diff-level check: confirm removal of the external opener dependency, environment branch, and invocation while retaining the same documentation URL.
Call-site check: confirm default, list, and refresh status paths all converge on the repaired empty-state behavior.
Unit-contract check: produce the empty state and assert the exact informational response containing both the external URL and internal documentation route.
Broader regression check, when the checkout is runnable: execute the command test file and verify configured-resource status tests remain successful.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the empty-state predicate or its browser-launch side effect cannot be established from before-state code.
Stop if removing navigation would violate an explicit requirement that this interaction launch a browser.
Stop if preserving the link target or another actionable handoff is impossible.
Do not claim end-to-end link integrity or successful internal documentation routing without a separate oracle for those destinations.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence bundle contains no PR body, review discussion, status checks, or reported test-run result.
The changed test verifies the returned URL text but does not resolve and inspect the shortened URL destination.
The changed test mentions `/docs` in the response but does not execute that command.
No runtime test execution result was established during this extraction; validation is grounded in the committed unit-test oracle and implementation diff.

unresolved_questions: Did CI or a local run execute the changed test successfully? The available GitHub bundle does not include status checks, and this extraction does not claim a runtime result.
Does `https://goo.gle/gemini-cli-docs-mcp` resolve to the intended live documentation destination? The implementation preserves the target, but the changed test only checks its literal presence.
Does the `/docs` command lead to the intended MCP documentation from this context? The change offers it as an alternative but adds no behavioral test for that route.

call_sites: The default `mcp` action delegates to the list action; the list action calls the shared status function, and refresh calls it after rediscovery. Therefore the empty-server branch governs multiple user-triggered status paths.
tests: Parent tests mocked the browser opener and separately asserted that sandbox execution did not open the URL while ordinary execution did open it.
The pinned test invokes the default command with an empty server map and asserts the exact unified informational response containing both the documentation URL and `/docs` guidance.
